title: HTML Document Integrity for Content Management
business: Content management systems that ingest user-provided HTML for display in internal dashboards.
problem: Unstructured or malformed HTML input leads to broken layout rendering and potential security risks when injected into the main document.
solution: Utilizing the HTML document structure and standard element definitions to sanitize and validate incoming content against defined content models.
steps: Define a strict subset of allowed HTML elements based on the specification's content models.
Parse the incoming raw string into a DOM tree to identify structural errors.
Strip elements that violate the intended content model or contain prohibited attributes.
Serialize the sanitized DOM tree back into a clean HTML string for storage.
outcome: Consistent document rendering and reduced risk of cross-site scripting through structural validation.
limitation: The primary tradeoff is the overhead of parsing and rebuilding the DOM tree, which can be checked by monitoring the latency of the sanitization service during high-volume ingestion.
